blocks.title: False Lips and a Spiteful Tongue

texts.NIV84: Better a dry crust with peace and quiet than a house full of feasting, with strife.
texts.KJV: Better is a dry morsel, and quietness therewith, than an house full of sacrifices with strife.
texts.NKJV:
Better is a dry morsel with quietness,
Than a house full of feasting with strife.
texts.DRB: Better is a dry morsel with joy, than a house full of victims with strife.

texts.NIV84: A wise servant will rule over a disgraceful son, and will share the inheritance as one of the brothers.
texts.KJV: A wise servant shall have rule over a son that causeth shame, and shall have part of the inheritance among the brethren.
texts.NKJV:
A wise servant will rule over a son who causes shame,
And will share an inheritance among the brothers.
texts.DRB: A wise servant shall rule over foolish sons, and shall divide the inheritance among the brethren.

texts.NIV84: The crucible for silver and the furnace for gold, but the LORD tests the heart.
texts.KJV: The fining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold: but the Lord trieth the hearts.
texts.NKJV:
The refining pot is for silver and the furnace for gold,
But the Lord tests the hearts.
texts.DRB: As silver is tried by fire, and gold in the furnace: so the Lord trieth the hearts.

texts.NIV84: A wicked man listens to evil lips; a liar pays attention to a malicious tongue.
texts.KJV: A wicked doer giveth heed to false lips; and a liar giveth ear to a naughty tongue.
texts.NKJV:
An evildoer gives heed to false lips;
A liar listens eagerly to a spiteful tongue.
texts.DRB: The evil man obeyeth an unjust tongue: and the deceitful hearkeneth to lying lips.

texts.NIV84: He who mocks the poor shows contempt for their Maker; whoever gloats over disaster will not go unpunished.
texts.KJV: Whoso mocketh the poor reproacheth his Maker: and he that is glad at calamities shall not be unpunished.
texts.NKJV:
He who mocks the poor reproaches his Maker;
He who is glad at calamity will not go unpunished.
texts.DRB: He that despiseth the poor, reproacheth his Maker; and he that rejoiceth at another man's ruin, shall not be unpunished.

texts.NIV84: Children's children are a crown to the aged, and parents are the pride of their children.
texts.KJV: Children's children are the crown of old men; and the glory of children are their fathers.
texts.NKJV:
Children’s children are the crown of old men,
And the glory of children is their father.
texts.DRB: Children's children are the crown of old men: and the glory of children are their fathers.

texts.NIV84: Arrogant lips are unsuited to a fool- how much worse lying lips to a ruler!
texts.KJV: Excellent speech becometh not a fool: much less do lying lips a prince.
texts.NKJV:
Excellent speech is not becoming to a fool,
Much less lying lips to a prince.
texts.DRB: Eloquent words do not become a fool, nor lying lips a prince.

blocks.title: Stop Contention Before A Quarrel Starts

texts.NIV84: A bribe is a charm to the one who gives it; wherever he turns, he succeeds.
texts.KJV: A gift is as a precious stone in the eyes of him that hath it: whithersoever it turneth, it prospereth.
texts.NKJV:
A present is a precious stone in the eyes of its possessor;
Wherever he turns, he prospers.
texts.DRB: The expectation of him that expecteth, is a most acceptable jewel: whithersoever he turneth himself, he understandeth wisely.

texts.NIV84: He who covers over an offense promotes love, but whoever repeats the matter separates close friends.
texts.KJV: He that covereth a transgression seeketh love; but he that repeateth a matter separateth very friends.
texts.NKJV:
He who covers a transgression seeks love,
But he who repeats a matter separates friends.
texts.DRB: He that concealeth a transgression. seeketh friendships: he that repeateth it again, separateth friends.

texts.NIV84: A rebuke impresses a man of discernment more than a hundred lashes a fool.
texts.KJV: A reproof entereth more into a wise man than an hundred stripes into a fool.
texts.NKJV:
Rebuke is more effective for a wise man
Than a hundred blows on a fool.
texts.DRB: A reproof availeth more with a wise man, than a hundred stripes with a fool.

texts.NIV84: An evil man is bent only on rebellion; a merciless official will be sent against him.
texts.KJV: An evil man seeketh only rebellion: therefore a cruel messenger shall be sent against him.
texts.NKJV:
An evil man seeks only rebellion;
Therefore a cruel messenger will be sent against him.
texts.DRB: An evil man always seeketh quarrels: but a cruel angel shall be sent against him.

texts.NIV84: Better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs than a fool in his folly.
texts.KJV: Let a bear robbed of her whelps meet a man, rather than a fool in his folly.
texts.NKJV:
Let a man meet a bear robbed of her cubs,
Rather than a fool in his folly.
texts.DRB: It is better to meet a bear robbed of her whelps, than a fool trusting in his own folly.

texts.NIV84: If a man pays back evil for good, evil will never leave his house.
texts.KJV: Whoso rewardeth evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house.
texts.NKJV:
Whoever rewards evil for good,
Evil will not depart from his house.
texts.DRB: He that rendereth evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house.

texts.NIV84: Starting a quarrel is like breaching a dam; so drop the matter before a dispute breaks out.
texts.KJV: The beginning of strife is as when one letteth out water: therefore leave off contention, before it be meddled with.
texts.NKJV:
The beginning of strife is like releasing water;
Therefore stop contention before a quarrel starts.
texts.DRB: The beginning of quarrels is as when one letteth out water: before he suffereth reproach he forsaketh judgment.

blocks.title: A Friend Loves at All Times

texts.NIV84: Acquitting the guilty and condemning the innocent- the LORD detests them both.
texts.KJV: He that justifieth the wicked, and he that condemneth the just, even they both are abomination to the Lord.
texts.NKJV:
He who justifies the wicked, and he who condemns the just,
Both of them alike are an abomination to the Lord.
texts.DRB: He that justifieth the wicked, and he that condemneth the just, both are abominable before God.

texts.NIV84: Of what use is money in the hand of a fool, since he has no desire to get wisdom?
texts.KJV: Wherefore is there a price in the hand of a fool to get wisdom, seeing he hath no heart to it?
texts.NKJV:
Why is there in the hand of a fool the purchase price of wisdom,
Since he has no heart for it?
texts.DRB: What doth it avail a fool to have riches, seeing he cannot buy wisdom? He that maketh his house high, seeketh a downfall: and he that refuseth to learn, shall fall into evils.

texts.NIV84: A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.
texts.KJV: A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.
texts.NKJV:
A friend loves at all times,
And a brother is born for adversity.
texts.DRB: He that is a friend loveth at all times: and a brother is proved in distress.

texts.NIV84: A man lacking in judgment strikes hands in pledge and puts up security for his neighbor.
texts.KJV: A man void of understanding striketh hands, and becometh surety in the presence of his friend.
texts.NKJV:
A man devoid of understanding shakes hands in a pledge,
And becomes surety for his friend.
texts.DRB: A foolish man will clap hands, when he is surety for his friend.

blocks.title: A Deceitful Heart Finds No Good

texts.NIV84: He who loves a quarrel loves sin; he who builds a high gate invites destruction.
texts.KJV: He loveth transgression that loveth strife: and he that exalteth his gate seeketh destruction.
texts.NKJV:
He who loves transgression loves strife,
And he who exalts his gate seeks destruction.
texts.DRB: He that studieth discords, loveth quarrels: and he that exalteth his door, seeketh ruin.

texts.NIV84: A man of perverse heart does not prosper; he whose tongue is deceitful falls into trouble.
texts.KJV: He that hath a froward heart findeth no good: and he that hath a perverse tongue falleth into mischief.
texts.NKJV:
He who has a deceitful heart finds no good,
And he who has a perverse tongue falls into evil.
texts.DRB: He that is of a perverse heart, shall not find good: and he that perverteth his tongue, shall fall into evil.

texts.NIV84: To have a fool for a son brings grief; there is no joy for the father of a fool.
texts.KJV: He that begetteth a fool doeth it to his sorrow: and the father of a fool hath no joy.
texts.NKJV:
He who begets a scoffer does so to his sorrow,
And the father of a fool has no joy.
texts.DRB: A fool is born to his own disgrace: and even his father shall not rejoice in a fool.

texts.NIV84: A cheerful heart is good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.
texts.KJV: A merry heart doeth good like a medicine: but a broken spirit drieth the bones.
texts.NKJV:
A merry heart does good, like medicine,
But a broken spirit dries the bones.
texts.DRB: A joyful mind maketh age flourishing: a sorrowful spirit drieth up the bones.

texts.NIV84: A wicked man accepts a bribe in secret to pervert the course of justice.
texts.KJV: A wicked man taketh a gift out of the bosom to pervert the ways of judgment.
texts.NKJV:
A wicked man accepts a bribe behind the back
To pervert the ways of justice.
texts.DRB: The wicked man taketh gifts out of the bosom, that he may pervert the paths of judgment.

texts.NIV84: A discerning man keeps wisdom in view, but a fool's eyes wander to the ends of the earth.
texts.KJV: Wisdom is before him that hath understanding; but the eyes of a fool are in the ends of the earth.
texts.NKJV:
Wisdom is in the sight of him who has understanding,
But the eyes of a fool are on the ends of the earth.
texts.DRB: Wisdom shineth in the face of the wise: the eyes of fools are in the ends of the earth.

texts.NIV84: A foolish son brings grief to his father and bitterness to the one who bore him.
texts.KJV: A foolish son is a grief to his father, and bitterness to her that bare him.
texts.NKJV:
A foolish son is a grief to his father,
And bitterness to her who bore him.
texts.DRB: A foolish son is the anger of the father: and the sorrow of the mother that bore him.

texts.NIV84: It is not good to punish an innocent man, or to flog officials for their integrity.
texts.KJV: Also to punish the just is not good, nor to strike princes for equity.
texts.NKJV:
Also, to punish the righteous is not good,
Nor to strike princes for their uprightness.
texts.DRB: It is no good thing to do hurt to the just: nor to strike the prince, who judgeth right.

texts.NIV84: A man of knowledge uses words with restraint, and a man of understanding is even-tempered.
texts.KJV: He that hath knowledge spareth his words: and a man of understanding is of an excellent spirit.
texts.NKJV:
He who has knowledge spares his words,
And a man of understanding is of a calm spirit.
texts.DRB: He that setteth bounds to his words. is knowing and wise: and the man of understanding is of a precious spirit.

texts.NIV84: Even a fool is thought wise if he keeps silent, and discerning if he holds his tongue.
texts.KJV: Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise: and he that shutteth his lips is esteemed a man of understanding.
texts.NKJV:
Even a fool is counted wise when he holds his peace;
When he shuts his lips, he is considered perceptive.
texts.DRB: Even a fool, if he will hold his peace shall be counted wise: and if he close his lips, a man of understanding.
